statusDefinitions.implemented: Present, production-reachable, and backed by named verification evidence.
statusDefinitions.partial: Present but has a documented boundary, structural risk, or incomplete verification.
statusDefinitions.planned: Desired in the target architecture but not implemented.
statusDefinitions.accepted_exception: A deliberate divergence from the target pattern with a recorded reason and guard.
statusDefinitions.deprecated: Present only for migration or compatibility and should lose callers.
statusDefinitions.unknown: Not yet reviewed with enough evidence to classify.

gaps: The public library surface is intentionally broad and still needs periodic production-reachability triage.
Long-run resource budgets and reproducible minimized fuzz-corpus handling remain active work.
PdfDocument.cs remains a multi-thousand-line coordination surface. Content, text, writing, and encryption dependencies now follow their registered directions without changing the public document API.

The renderer necessarily re-executes graphics/text state as an accepted exception; content also temporarily depends upward on text-owned glyph decoding (#1318) and writer-owned number formatting (#1319).
Full PDF font-model completeness remains broader than the currently supported corpus, and two font lookup tables remain text-owned until #1320.

Extraction coverage remains a measured bound on text redaction completeness, not a proof of completeness. Redaction implementation is still path-owned as core-text until #1321 establishes a real component boundary.

Sixty-seven method-level redaction assertions still carry reviewed exceptions; generic no-independent-oracle entries remain an assurance backlog. The current ownership model assigns zero retained symbols to core-redaction until #1321.
Platform signature trust behavior remains at delivery-layer action boundaries by design; structural and conformance validation remains distinct from platform trust evaluation.
Renderer partials remain several thousand lines each and re-execute graphics/text state as an accepted architectural exception.

PdfViewerControl remains a large partial-class family after single-page render generation, cancellation-source, and bitmap-LRU lifetime moved to SinglePageRenderLifetime. Single-page and continuous caches now have disjoint documented ownership and typed telemetry, while continuous scheduling, layout, interaction, and accessibility boundaries still need measured decomposition.

Program.cs remains a 2,218-line command host after save-size-report, command-metadata, fill-form, typed unredact, and safe-copy policy adapter extractions; the remaining command boundaries still need measured decomposition and duplicate-policy analysis.
The main window view model remains the dominant state/orchestration hub.

Production and tests now share one required MainWindowViewModel dependency contract; tests provide deterministic headless defaults through a named factory, while production remains owned by the validated application composition root.
Debug-only scripting and platform activation require conservative reachability seeds.

Scripting and save workflows still share workspace state; constructor composition, thumbnail lifetime, search-index lifetime, search execution lifetime and source selection, annotation mutation transactions, page-image export transactions, split-request parsing, redaction mark/apply/save transactions, document-close reset phases, document-open stages, command composition, and viewport state now have explicit owners or contracts.

Reachability is compile-time evidence: observed XAML, dependency-injection, callback, interface-dispatch, static-constructor, and test-reference mechanisms are modeled and mutation-tested, while unobserved runtime mechanisms remain explicit blind spots.

The coherent artifact gate now schema-validates and hash-binds inventory, topology, coupling, conformance, and diagrams, while coupling scope is derived from shipping inventory. All observed component edges are classified; four remaining Core direction/ownership defects are explicit issue-linked exceptions (#1318-#1321), and unresolved type edges remain confined to explicit non-shipping ownership gaps. XAML reports zero untyped first-party binding paths and zero unresolved typed member segments after #1305.

concerns.name: Main-window state and workflow concentration
concerns.desiredState: The main window is a small workspace shell; feature state, cancellation, commands, and workflow policy have explicit owners and contract tests.
symptoms: MainWindowViewModel.cs is 2,985 lines before its additional partials; search-index and search-execution lifecycles, annotation mutation and page-image export transactions, staged document-open orchestration, workflow-grouped command composition, thumbnail-session ownership, page/view/zoom viewport ownership, and one required composition contract are complete, but other workflow ownership remains concentrated.

Production uses an explicit validated service factory, tests use a named factory with explicit overrides and production-matching contracts, and design-time XAML no longer creates a second service graph.

Document, editing, redaction, security, and background work still share mutable state; thumbnail, search-request, annotation-mutation, and page/view/zoom viewport lifetimes now have explicit owners, with same-page and same-mode feedback made idempotent.
rootCauseQuestions: Which state belongs to the document session, viewport, or a feature workflow?
Which partials communicate through shared fields rather than explicit contracts?
Which remaining workflows need a state owner rather than another partial-file split?
Which extractions reduce coupling rather than merely move lines?

concerns.name: Outsized implementation units and responsibility accumulation
concerns.desiredState: Large files are justified by cohesive generated/table-driven behavior or decomposed along measured state/contract seams, with no duplicate engines introduced.
symptoms: Several production files exceed 2,000 lines, including renderer partials, the CLI host, ContentStreamWalker, PdfDocument, PdfViewerControl, and MainWindowViewModel.
Line count alone cannot distinguish irreducible PDF state machinery from mixed workflow ownership.
deterministicDiscovery: rg -n 'class |partial class |switch |case ' Excise.Rendering Excise.Cli Excise.Core/Document Excise.Avalonia/Controls
rootCauseQuestions: Is size caused by a cohesive state machine, unrelated responsibilities, duplicated policy, or generated/tabular data?
Which types have high fan-in/fan-out or share mutable state?
Would extraction create a second state machine or clarify an existing contract?
Which large test/tool files are off the shipping graph and therefore lower priority?

concerns.name: Architecture and security gate baseline integrity
concerns.desiredState: Every t0 architecture/security gate passes for reviewed reasons, and mutations prove each gate detects the defect class it claims to detect.
symptoms: Configuration-specific PublicApi snapshots can create duplicate assembly identities unless normalization remains mutation-tested.
Redaction test edits can reintroduce self-oracle-only assertions unless per-method oracle loss remains mutation-tested.
rootCauseQuestions: Does a future unwired delta represent a real configuration-only API, an assembly-key normalization defect, or stale triage?
For each future redaction diagnostic, what exact property is asserted and which independent instrument can observe it?
Can the gate distinguish implementation gaps from checker false positives without blanket allowlisting?

concerns.name: Dependency advisory acquisition is not deterministic
concerns.desiredState: PR, scheduled, and release scans acquire current advisory data in a writable isolated cache, emit machine-readable evidence, and distinguish unavailable data from a clean result.
symptoms: dotnet list package --vulnerable reports NU1900 for App and App.Tests because the NuGet advisory cache cannot refresh.
The command still prints no vulnerable packages, which can be misread as a complete clean audit.
rootCauseQuestions: Why is only part of the restore graph attempting a denied cache write?
Which cache/environment contract works both in sandboxed development and CI?
Should advisory acquisition failure be a separate hard-fail status from vulnerable/clean?
How does this work align with the broader supply-chain epic without putting network checks in t0?

concerns.name: .NET analyzer, warning, and suppression policy
concerns.desiredState: One central policy enables an agreed analyzer level; new warnings fail in scoped projects; suppressions are narrow, justified, and verified on all target platforms.
symptoms: There is no central Directory.Build.props analysis policy.
CA1416 is suppressed across the entire desktop project.
The current build can succeed with NU1900 warnings despite documentation expecting a clean build.
rootCauseQuestions: Which warnings are product defects, cross-platform false positives, third-party rollups, or environment failures?
Which projects can enforce warnings first without forcing blanket suppressions?
Can CA1416 be replaced by platform guards and source-level suppressions?
Which analyzer findings overlap reachability and should share one root-cause issue?

concerns.name: Narrative architecture status can drift from implementation
concerns.desiredState: Current/target component status, dependencies, workflow ownership, verification, and known gaps live in the checked JSON registry; narrative docs explain concepts and link to it.
symptoms: Architecture, design, implementation-plan, and status claims are spread across documents and registries with overlapping authority.
Static diagrams and prose do not fail when project dependencies or evidence paths change.
rootCauseQuestions: Which claims belong in timeless narrative versus status-bearing registry data?
Which component boundaries can be verified from project references, paths, and reachability?
Which target relationships need an issue before they can be marked planned?
What diagram granularity remains readable and decision-useful?

concerns.name: Source provenance and independent-implementation assurance
concerns.desiredState: Every current source and vendored-data family has evidence-backed lineage, attribution, and a reviewed retain-or-replace decision without overstating clean-room status.
symptoms: Legacy v1 directly used PdfPig, PDFsharp, and PDFtoImage while the current stack removed those packages.
Historical planning proposed borrowing several implementation families, so package removal alone does not prove clean-room provenance.
The Avalonia dispatcher scheduler explicitly records an adapted third-party lineage.
deterministicDiscovery: rg -n -i 'adapted|vendored|derived|PdfPig|PDFsharp|PDFtoImage|ReactiveUI' Excise.Core Excise.Rendering Excise.App docs LICENSES.md
rootCauseQuestions: Which files are specification-derived facts versus copyrightable implementation expression?
Which current code descends from earlier Excise implementations that used external libraries?
Which adapted code should be retained with attribution versus independently replaced?
How should new vendoring or material clone introduction fail deterministically?
